==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|frome||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|from|t=from}}, from {{inh|en|ang|from}}, {{m|ang|fram|t=forward, from}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*fram}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*fram|t=forward, from, away}}. Cognate with {{cog|osx|fram|t=from}} and {{cog|goh|fram|t=from}}, {{cog|da|frem|t=forth, forward}}, {{cog|da|fra|t=from}}, {{cog|sv|fram|t=forth, forward}}, {{cog|sv|från|t=from}}, {{cog|nn|fram|t=forward}}, {{cog|nn|frå|t=from}}, {{cog|is|fram|t=forward, on}}, {{cog|is|frá|t=from}}, {{cog|sq|pre}}, {{m|sq|prej}}. More at {{m|en|fro}}.

* {{hyph|en|from}}

===Preposition===
{{en-head|prep}}

# {{n-g|Used to indicate [[source]] or [[provenance]].}}
#: {{ux|en|Paul is '''from''' New Zealand.}}
#: {{ux|en|I got a letter '''from''' my brother.}}
#: {{ux|en|You can't get all your news '''from''' the Internet.}}
#* {{RQ:Jefferies Amateur Poacher|chapter=II|passage=Orion hit a rabbit once; but though sore wounded it got to the bury, and, struggling in, the arrow caught the side of the hole and was drawn out.{{nb...}}. Ikey the blacksmith had forged us a spearhead after a sketch '''from''' a picture of a Greek warrior; and a rake-handle served as a shaft.}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=12|passage=There were many wooden chairs for the bulk of his visitors, and two wicker armchairs with red cloth cushions for superior people. '''From''' the packing-cases had emerged some Indian clubs,{{nb...}}, and all these articles{{...}}made a scattered and untidy decoration that Mrs. Clough assiduously dusted and greatly cherished.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-29|volume=407|issue=8842|page=72–3
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/international/science-and-technology/21580133-how-microbes-promote-liver-cancer-overweight-punch-gut A punch in the gut]
|passage=Mostly, the microbiome is beneficial. It helps with digestion and enables people to extract a lot more calories '''from''' their food than would otherwise be possible. Research over the past few years, however, has implicated it in diseases from atherosclerosis to asthma to autism.}}
# Originating at (a year, time, etc.)
#: {{ux|en|This manuscript is '''from''' the 1980s.}}
# {{n-g|Used to indicate a starting point or [[initial]] [[reference]].}}
#: {{ux|en|He had books piled '''from''' floor to ceiling.}}
#: {{ux|en|He departed yesterday '''from''' Chicago.}}
#: {{ux|en|This figure has been changed '''from''' a one to a seven.}}
#: {{ux|en|Face away '''from''' the wall!}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=8|passage=The humor of my proposition appealed more strongly to Miss Trevor than I had looked for, and '''from''' that time forward she became her old self again; for, even after she had conquered her love for the Celebrity, the mortification of having been jilted by him remained.}}
## {{n-g|Indicating a starting [[point in time]].}}
##: {{ux|en|The working day runs '''from''' 9 am to 5 pm.}}
##: {{ux|en|Tickets are available '''from''' 17th July.}}
##: {{ux|en|The store will be open '''from''' nine in the morning, but I’ll be at home '''from''' Wed. evening (on).}}
##: {{ux|en|'''From''' the time they were young, Spartans were trained for war. }}
## {{n-g|Indicating a starting point on a [[range]] or [[scale]].}}
##: {{ux|en|Rate your pain '''from''' 1 to 10.}}
##: {{ux|en|Start counting '''from''' 1.}}
## {{n-g|Indicating a starting point on an [[array]] or [[gamut]] of [[conceptual]] [[variation]]s.}}
##: {{ux|en|You can study anything '''from''' math to literature.}}
## With reference to the location or position of a speaker or other observer or vantage point.
##: {{ux|en|It's hard to tell '''from''' here.}}
##: {{ux|en|Try to see it '''from''' his point of view.}}
##: {{ux|en|The bomb went off just 100 yards '''from''' where they were standing.}}
##: {{ux|en|'''From''' the top of the lighthouse you can just see the mainland.}}
## {{lb|en|MLE}} {{n-g|Indicates a starting state of the [[predicament]] of the subject.}} {{synonym of|en|[[since]] [[being]]}}.
##: {{ux|en|I’ve been doing this '''from''' [[pickney]].}}
# {{n-g|Indicating [[removal]] or [[separation]].}}
#: {{ux|en|After twenty minutes, remove the cake '''from''' the oven.}}
#: {{ux|en|The general was ousted '''from''' power.}}
#: {{ux|en|He knuckled the sleep '''from''' his eyes.}}
## {{lb|en|mathematics|chiefly|British|not in formal use}} {{n-g|Denoting a subtraction operation.}}
##: {{ux|en|20 '''from''' 31 leaves 11.}}
# {{n-g|Indicating [[exclusion]].}}
#: {{ux|en|She was barred '''from''' entering.}}
#: {{ux|en|A parasol protects '''from''' the sun.}}
# {{n-g|Indicating [[differentiation]].}}
#: {{ux|en|Your opinions differ '''from''' mine.}}
#: {{ux|en|He knows right '''from''' wrong.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=May-June|author=[http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/katrina-g-claw Katrina G. Claw]
|title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/feature/2013/3/rapid-evolution-in-eggs-and-sperm Rapid Evolution in Eggs and Sperm]
|volume=101|issue=3|magazine=w:American Scientist
|passage=In plants, the ability to recognize self '''from''' nonself plays an important role in fertilization, because self-fertilization will result in less diverse offspring than fertilization with pollen from another individual.}}
# Produced with or out of (a substance or material).
#: {{ux|en|It's made '''from''' pure gold.}}
# {{n-g|Used to indicate causation}}; because of, as a result of.
#: {{ux|en|Too many people die '''from''' breast cancer.}}
